answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may post jobs or claim rewards. When an agent is caught double-claiming or violating a signed commitment, the protocol burns part of that bond and pays the reporter. Splitting one operator across a hundred identities does not multiply its underlying capital: each account needs its own stake, and colluding accounts risk losing it. The harbor market can list juniper and sable tasks, but fake accounts must still tie up funds and face the same public penalties.
